Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Greenville-Spartanburg SC
647 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Snowfall totals for tonight/early Friday have increased slightly
across the high elevations of southwest NC, but sub-Winter Wx
Advisory conditions are still expected.

Wind gusts were bumped up slightly for tonight, but should remain
below Wind Advisory criteria.

Aviation discussion updated for the 00z TAFs.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1. Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue through
Friday. Light wintry precipitation is anticipated near the
Tennessee border tonight into Friday, with some accumulations
expected over mainly the higher elevations.
2. Temperatures warm quickly ahead of the next cold front this
weekend, which will bring more gusty winds and a quick shot of
rain on Sunday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Key message 1: Gusty winds redevelop this afternoon and continue
through Friday. Light wintry precipitation is anticipated near
the Tennessee border tonight into Friday, with some accumulations
expected over mainly the higher elevations.

A sprawling upper low/attendant trough currently centered over the
TN Valley is forecast to continue gradual intensification as it
lifts into the central Appalachians by Friday morning. Secondary
surface low development is forecast over the central Apps/northern
Mid-Atlantic this afternoon into tonight, increasing the surface
gradient across the region and resulting in gusty SW winds across
our CWA. Peak wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph are expected this evening
into the early part of the overnight, with occasional gusts
of around 40 mph expected across the high elevations as well as
portions of the NC Piedmont. These winds will be capable of blowing
around loose objects as well as cause sporadic power outages.

A cold front will pivot across the CWA in advance of the upper
trough from late this afternoon into the evening, possibly bringing
some light precip into mainly the western part of the CWA. Precip
chances further increase to likely/categorical across the mountains
this evening as a deformation zone brushes the western part of the
CWA. Snow levels will be steadily dropping during this time within
the cold advection regime and under cold core aloft. The potential
for wintry precip will increase this evening, mainly across the
higher elevations, with some light wintry weather possibly reaching
the valley floors by daybreak Friday. Due to the track of the
cyclone, low level flow in the cold advection regime is forecast
to remain largely W/SW, so upslope lift will generally be minimal,
and most of the impetus for rising motion will be due to synoptic
forcing. However, the SW flow will result in a small area of upslope
enhancement across southwest NC, and accumulating snowfall to the
tune of mostly 1-2" is forecast across the higher elevations of
western Graham and Macon Counties tonight into early Friday. This
is insufficient for a Winter Wx Advisory, but a Special Weather
Statement highlighting the potential for some slick high elevation
roads in these areas appears warranted. While mostly snow/rain
is forecast, model forecast soundings do depict establishment
of a warm nose across the southern Appalachians overnight, so a
transition to light freezing rain or drizzle is possible across
the NC counties bordering TN...even across the valleys.

Gusty winds continue through much of Friday, albeit steadily
diminishing through the day. While conditions through tonight will
be noticeably gusty, conditions are expected to fall a bit shy of
Wind Advisory criteria. Otherwise, min temps through Friday night
will be around 5 degrees below climo, while max temps Friday are
forecast to be around 10 degrees below normal under cold advection
and some lingering cloud cover.


Key message 2: Temperatures warm quickly ahead of the next cold front
this weekend, which will bring more gusty winds and a quick shot
of rain on Sunday.

An intensifying short wave trough is forecast to eject from
the central Conus across the TN and OH Valleys on Sunday,
with a resultant deepening cyclone forecast across the Ohio
Valley. Attendant fast-moving cold front is forecast to sweep
across our area late in the day, with sufficient Gulf inflow and
low-level forcing to support categorical PoPs across the entire area
Sunday evening. Current indications are that rainfall amounts of
0.25-0.5" will occur across the western half of the CWA, with more
like 0.1-0.33" across the east. Temperatures warming quickly in
the warm advection in advance of the front will ensure all precip
falls as liquid, although a brief period of northwest flow/upslope
snow showers will be possible across the higher elevations along
the TN/NC border late Sunday night. Dry conditions are otherwise
forecast Monday through Thursday, with temperatures mainly forecast
to be within 2-3 degrees of climo.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
At KCLT and elsewhere: Wrap-around moisture associated with
large low pressure system that is drifting toward of the area
will continue to result in mainly MVFR cigs tonight. There may
be breaks in the low cloud deck at times overnight thru Friday
morning, but overall, the clouds will stubbornly hold on well
thru the day. Rain and drizzle is gradually tapering off, with a
wintry mix of mainly snow, but possibly some sleet and freezing
drizzle in the mountains near the TN border overnight. That precip
is expected to be light and not impact any of the TAF sites.

Meanwhile, winds have turned out of the SW and become gusty
again. The winds will be strongest this evening thru about 06z
(with frequent gusts around or even higher than 30 kt), then weaken
slightly thru Friday morning. A second uptick in gusts likely again
in the aftn, before finally starting subside and lose gustiness
mid to late Friday evening.

Outlook: Dry and VFR returns Saturday before a cold front brings
a brief shot of rain and associated restrictions Sunday afternoon
into Sunday night. Drier conditions return early next week.
